proofs.proof_tex:
Take \(X=\{1\}\), \(Y=\{3\}\), and \(\mathfrak G_{\star}=\{D_A,D_B\}\). By \(\mathrm{lem{:}teh\text{-}sufficient\text{-}criterion}\), the first graphical requirement forbids a proper semidirected path from \(X\) to \(Y\) beginning with an undirected edge. Both \(D_A\) and \(D_B\) are DAGs, so neither contains an undirected edge and this requirement holds vacuously.

For the pairwise part of that criterion, in \(D_A\) node \(1\) is an ancestor of node \(3\), while in \(D_B\) it is not. Hence the relevant treatment-ancestor sets are
\[
 A_A=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_A}(Y)=\{1\},
 \qquad
 A_B=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_B}(Y)=\varnothing.
\]
Every chain component of a DAG is a singleton. In particular, the pertinent parent sets disagree because
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_A}(1)=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_B}(1)=\{3,4\}.
\]
Thus the parent-set alternative in the cited criterion fails. For its reweighted-graph alternative, the ancestral margin relevant to outcome \(3\) in \(D_A\) has vertex set \(\{1,2,3\}\) and arrows \(1\to3\leftarrow2\), whereas \(A_B=\varnothing\) and the corresponding ancestral margin in \(D_B\) is the singleton graph on \(\{3\}\). Graphs with different vertex sets cannot be Markov equivalent. The second alternative therefore also fails, so the sufficient graphical criterion is not satisfied.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}four\text{-}node\text{-}cross\text{-}mec\text{-}witness}\), \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is accepted, \(p_{\star}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I_{\star}}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{16}\), and
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_{\star})=\frac{13}{20}\neq\frac12=T_{D_B,+1}(p_{\star}).
\]
For completeness, the displayed formula for \(p_{\star}\) also gives its coordinate heights directly. Each of its four numerator factors is \(2/3\) or \(4/3\). The product of the four associated signs
\[
 (s_1s_3)(s_1s_4)(s_2s_3)(-s_2s_4)=-1
\]
shows that exactly one or three factors are \(4/3\). Since \(16(1-3^{-4})=1280/81\), every cell probability is therefore
\[
 \frac{2}{80}=\frac1{40}
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \frac{8}{80}=\frac1{10}.
\]
Their reduced numerator and denominator bit lengths are at most \(6\). The defining bounds \(H\geq0\), \(d\geq1\), \(c_0\geq1\), \(m=16\), and \(r\geq1\) imply
\[
 B_{\mathrm{cert}}
 =2^{(H+1)(2d+2)^{2^{c_0(m+r)}}}>6.
\]
Thus \(p_{\star}\) occurs in the prescribed bounded rational enumeration.

Let \(D_0\) be whichever of \(D_A,D_B\) is first in the canonical graph order, and let \(D\) be the other graph. If every normal form were zero, \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) applied at \(p_{\star}\) would force the two displayed intervention probabilities to be equal, a contradiction. Hence at least one normal form is nonzero and \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) enters its rational-search branch. Because that enumeration is canonical and contains \(p_{\star}\), it returns a qualifying separator no later than the check of \(p_{\star}\). By \(\mathrm{lem{:}bounded\text{-}search\text{-}certificate\text{-}soundness}\), every such returned table is a sound exact-oracle separator. Independently of which qualifying table appears first, \(p_{\star}\) itself is the asserted replayable separator with values \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). This one certified query is outside the sufficient graphical region and is nevertheless resolved as nonidentification, proving the claimed strictness in decision-output coverage.

Fix \(\mathfrak u\), its equality-branch circuit, and \(P\) as in the statement. Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives
\[
 P_z>0\qquad(z\in\Omega).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), every recorded denominator is a finite product of observed marginal probabilities. Each marginal is a nonempty sum of positive cells, and hence
\[
 B_{D,y}(P)>0\qquad(D\in\mathfrak D,\ y).
\]
There are finitely many pairs \((D,y)\). Polynomial continuity therefore supplies an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(P\) on which all recorded denominators remain positive. A quotient of polynomials with nonvanishing denominator is continuously differentiable, so \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on \(U\), with derivative \(J_{\tau}\).

For each cell \(z\), let \(e_z\in\mathbb R^m\) be its coordinate vector, and define
\[
 W_i=e_{Z_i}-P.
\]
The independent multinomial sampling assumption gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PW_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P(W_iW_i^{\mathsf T})
 =\operatorname{diag}(P)-PP^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma_P,
\]
and the empirical-table definition gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i.
\]
The vectors \(W_i\) have finite support, so \(\mathbb E_P\lVert W_i\rVert^2<\infty\). Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}multivariate\text{-}iid\text{-}clt}\) yields
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P),
\]
where singularity of \(\Sigma_P\) is allowed. Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat p_n-P\rVert_2^2
 =\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_P)}{n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so \(\widehat p_n\to P\) in probability. Since \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(P\),
\[
 \Pr_P(\widehat p_n\in U)\longrightarrow1.
\]
In particular, the denominator event in \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\) has probability tending to one.

Continuous differentiability on \(U\) gives, whenever \(h\to0\) with \(P+h\in U\),
\[
 \tau(P+h)=\tau(P)+J_{\tau}(P)h+r(h),
 \qquad
 \frac{\lVert r(h)\rVert}{\lVert h\rVert}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The central limit theorem implies \(\sqrt n\lVert\widehat p_n-P\rVert=O_P(1)\), while consistency implies \(\Pr_P(\widehat p_n\in U)\to1\). Hence
\[
 \sqrt n\,r(\widehat p_n-P)=o_P(1)
\]
on an event whose probability tends to one. This is exactly the local remainder conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem{:}multivariate\text{-}delta\text{-}method}\). Moreover \(U\) is contained in the denominator event, so \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) whenever \(\widehat p_n\in U\). Therefore
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P)\}
 =J_{\tau}(P)\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)+o_P(1)
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]

The maps
\[
 p\longmapsto\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 p\longmapsto J_{\tau}(p)
\]
are continuous at \(P\), the latter because \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on \(U\). Therefore, on an event whose probability tends to one,
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n\xrightarrow{P}\Sigma_P,
 \qquad
 J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P).
\]
Matrix multiplication is continuous, and the off-event value of \(\widehat V_n\) is again irrelevant with probability tending to one. Hence
\[
 \widehat V_n
 =J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\widehat\Sigma_nJ_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}
 \xrightarrow{P}
 J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}.
\]

Because the circuit is on the equality branch, all its normal forms are zero by \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\). The soundness result \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 \tau_y(P)=T_{D,y}(P)\qquad(D\in\mathfrak D).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) and the Markov conclusion used in that lemma, this common value is the causal intervention cell \(P_x(Y=y)\), not an observed regression functional.

Finally assume \(\sigma_y^2>0\). The scalar marginal of the multivariate limit and variance consistency give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,y}-P_x(Y=y)\}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\sigma_y^2),
 \qquad
 \widehat V_{n,yy}\xrightarrow{P}\sigma_y^2>0.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}slutsky\text{-}scalar}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,y}-P_x(Y=y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}}}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The points \(-1.96\) and \(1.96\) have zero probability under the standard normal law. Therefore the limiting coverage of the stated interval is
\[
 \Pr\{-1.96\leq Z\leq1.96\}
 =2\Phi(1.96)-1
 =0.9500042097\ldots,
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
which proves every assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(k\geq 1\), let \(U=\prod_{j=1}^k(a_j,b_j)\) be a nonempty open box with rational endpoints, and let \(\phi:U\to\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) be a rational map defined over \(\mathbb Q\), with every coordinate denominator nonzero on \(U\). Fix \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and an outcome cell \(y\). Suppose that
\[
 F_{D,y}(\phi(t))=\frac{N(t)}{Q(t)},
\]
where \(N,Q\in\mathbb Q[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\), \(Q\) is nonzero throughout \(U\), and \(N\) is a nonzero polynomial of total degree at most \(e\). For arbitrary sets \(S_j\subset(a_j,b_j)\cap\mathbb Q\) of \(e+1\) distinct points, some \(t\in\prod_{j=1}^kS_j\) satisfies \(F_{D,y}(\phi(t))\neq0\). Consequently at most \((e+1)^k\) exact grid evaluations produce a table \(p^{\dagger}=\phi(t)\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) for which \(T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose the finite sets \(S_j\) as in the statement. We first prove the elementary grid claim
\[
 N\neq0,\quad \deg N\leq e
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 N\text{ does not vanish on all of }\prod_{j=1}^kS_j.
\]
For \(k=1\), repeated use of the factor theorem shows that a polynomial having the \(e+1\) distinct elements of \(S_1\) as roots is divisible by their product, which has degree \(e+1\); hence a polynomial of degree at most \(e\) with those roots is zero. Assume the claim for \(k-1\) variables and write
\[
 N(t_1,\ldots,t_k)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{e}N_{\ell}(t_1,\ldots,t_{k-1})t_k^{\ell}.
\]
If \(N\) vanished on the whole grid, then for each fixed \(t'\in\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}S_j\), the univariate polynomial \(N(t',\,\cdot\,)\), of degree at most \(e\), would vanish at all \(e+1\) points of \(S_k\). The one-variable argument would give \(N_{\ell}(t')=0\) for every \(\ell\). Each \(N_{\ell}\) has total degree at most \(e\), so the induction hypothesis would give \(N_{\ell}=0\) for every \(\ell\), contradicting \(N\neq0\). Thus there is a grid point \(t\) with \(N(t)\neq0\).

Every coordinate of this \(t\) is rational. Since \(\phi\) is defined over \(\mathbb Q\) and its coordinate denominators do not vanish on \(U\), \(p^{\dagger}=\phi(t)\) belongs to \(\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\). The range condition on \(\phi\) gives \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\). Also \(Q(t)\neq0\), and therefore
\[
 F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})=\frac{N(t)}{Q(t)}\neq0.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\), all cells of \(p^{\dagger}\) are positive. By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), every factor recorded in \(B_{D,y}\) and \(B_{D_0,y}\) is an observed marginal probability, hence a nonempty sum of positive cells. Thus
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})>0.
\]
Using \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\) and dividing by this positive product gives
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})-T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})}
 {B_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})}\neq0.
\]
The grid has exactly \((e+1)^k\) points, proving the evaluation bound and the conclusion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), if
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0
 \quad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D\text{ and every outcome cell }y,
\]
then the equality output of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) is sound: for every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)
 \quad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D\text{ and }y.
\]
Thus \(\tau(p)=(T_{D_0,y}(p))_y\) is the common represented-DAG intervention law, and each asserted equality has a finite exactly checkable real-Nullstellensatz and saturation certificate.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted \(\mathfrak u\), a table \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), a graph \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and an outcome cell \(y\). Put \(L=J_{\mathcal I}:s^{\infty}\). By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\), normalization and every oracle-one generator vanish at \(p\), so
\[
 h(p)=0\qquad\text{for every }h\in J_{\mathcal I}.
\]
Strict positivity gives \(p_z>0\) for every cell \(z\). By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), each factor recorded in any \(B_{D',y'}\) is an observed marginal probability and hence is a nonempty sum of positive cells. Therefore
\[
 B_{D',y'}(p)>0\quad\text{for all }D',y',
 \qquad s(p)\neq0.
\]
If \(h\in L\), the definition of saturation supplies an integer \(N\geq0\) such that \(s^Nh\in J_{\mathcal I}\). Evaluation at \(p\) yields \(s(p)^Nh(p)=0\), and division by \(s(p)^N\neq0\) yields \(h(p)=0\). Hence \(p\) belongs to the real variety of \(L\).

The zero normal form is, by the defining property of the canonical basis used in \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}\), equivalent to \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\). By \(\mathrm{def{:}saturated\text{-}real\text{-}radical}\), every polynomial in \(K_{\mathcal I}=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{L}\) vanishes on the real variety of \(L\). Consequently
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)=0.
\]
The cross-signature identity and denominator positivity now give
\[
 0=A_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)-A_{D_0,y}(p)B_{D,y}(p)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{A_{D,y}(p)}{B_{D,y}(p)}
 =\frac{A_{D_0,y}(p)}{B_{D_0,y}(p)}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), the two ratios are \(T_{D,y}(p)\) and \(T_{D_0,y}(p)\). By \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\), \(p\) is Markov to every represented DAG, so these truncated factorizations are the corresponding DAG intervention cells rather than arbitrary regression functionals. Since \(D,y,p\) were arbitrary, \(\tau\) is common on the exact-oracle model. Finally, \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}size}\) supplies the finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities for each zero normal form, with exact verification polynomial in their expanded length.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the bounded rational-table search on a nonzero-normal-form branch of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) contains at most
\[
 2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
coordinate descriptions. Every candidate test is decidable by exact rational arithmetic. Whenever the search returns \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\), one has \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and, for at least one outcome cell \(y\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger});
\]
hence the two represented DAG intervention vectors differ.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
An integer of bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) has at most \(2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}\) signed descriptions under the fixed encoding. Describing one reduced rational coordinate by a signed numerator and a positive denominator therefore uses at most
\[
 2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
pairs. Taking the Cartesian product over the \(m\) cells gives at most
\[
 \left(2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\right)^m
 =2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
table descriptions. Positivity and normalization, coprimality, and duplicate removal can only decrease this number.

For a rational candidate, normalization, cell positivity, all oracle-one polynomial equalities, every oracle-zero strict sum-of-squares inequality, every recorded denominator, and every signature are decidable by exact integer arithmetic after clearing positive denominators. Thus the membership and failed-signature tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\) are exact.

If the procedure returns \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\), its return test gives
\[
 p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega},
 \qquad F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\neq0
\]
for some \(y\). As in the proof of equality-branch soundness, strict positivity and \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) imply
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})>0.
\]
The cross-signature definition then yields
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})-T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})}
 {B_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger})}\neq0.
\]
One unequal coordinate makes the two intervention vectors unequal, proving soundness of every returned separator and the stated finite-search bound.

proposed.statement: Theorem 1 (effect-specific rational-positive separation). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and every outcome cell \(y\), if \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), then there exists \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) whose reduced coordinate numerators and denominators have bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) such that \(F_{D,y}(p^{\dagger})\ne0\). Conversely, \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\) implies \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved equality direction and the proved rational-chart reduction into the still-open separation theorem without changing its claim.

proposed.statement: Theorem 2 (SparseSIM-ID completeness). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), under Theorem 1, \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminates after at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) exact rational-table checks and returns exactly one of two mutually exclusive certificates: either one observable arithmetic circuit \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with identities proving \(T_{D,y}=T_{D_0,y}\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) for every \(D,y\), or \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\) with \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and \((T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\ne(T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\). The first branch occurs if and only if the intervention law is common to every represented DAG. On tied SA-MPDAG families this is a strict decision-theoretic tightening of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo: every query passing their sufficient graphical test is on the equality branch, while every query failing that test is still decided by an equality certificate or a rational positive separator. When \(\mathfrak G\) is a singleton and \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) equals its full positive Markov model, the decision agrees with Perkovic's single-MPDAG criterion and generalized truncated factorization.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Record the proved equality-branch and bounded-search subresults as direct dependencies of the completeness claim; the claim itself is unchanged and remains open at rational-positive separation.

proposed.statement: Corollary 1 (strictness relative to Teh--Sadeghi--Soo). For the certified input \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) and query \(P_{Y_1=+1}(Y_3=+1)\), the sufficient graphical conditions of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo are not satisfied, whereas \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) returns a rational positive separator; the table \(p_{\star}\) is an explicit admissible separator with graphwise values \(13/20\) under \(D_A\) and \(1/2\) under \(D_B\). Hence SparseSIM-ID strictly tightens that sufficient-only test on certified tied-sparsest inputs by resolving at least one query on which it is undecided.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the unresolved completeness dependency by the two proved algorithmic soundness lemmas actually used by the strict finite witness proof.

proposed.statement: Theorem 3 (fixed-input plug-in inference). Fix one finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), fix its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\). Every recorded denominator is positive at \(P\), so the rational circuit \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_n\) has probability tending to one, and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right)\). Moreover, \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\sigma_y^2>0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}/n}\) has limiting coverage \(0.9500042097\ldots\) for \(P_x(Y=y)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Use the proved equality-branch soundness lemma directly, so fixed-input inference no longer depends on the unresolved global rational-separation theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Show that every intervention signature outside the saturated real-radical ideal is nonzero at a strictly positive rational table satisfying all bit-one equalities and all bit-zero inequalities, with coordinate height at most the declared certificate bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: Real-radical nonmembership can be witnessed on an equality component disjoint from the positive exact-oracle chamber containing the supplied rational feasibility point. Saturation excludes zero factors but neither selects signs nor guarantees a rational point on the separating component.
open_obligations.attempted: The real-variety evaluation argument proves the converse. Rational approximation fails because it need not preserve the conditional-independence equations. The new chart lemma gives a finite rational-grid separator whenever a rational open-box chart with nonzero pulled-back signature is available, but the frozen hypotheses do not supply such a chart on every detected component or the advertised global height bound.
open_obligations.partial_result: The membership-to-equality direction is completely proved by \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\). In addition, \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\text{-}grid\text{-}separator\text{-}on\text{-}chart}\) proves the constructive implication on any rational open-box chart whose pullback of \(F_{D,y}\) is nonzero: a grid of at most \((e+1)^k\) rational points contains a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator. The remaining step is precisely to prove that such a chart exists for every \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\) and that its induced coordinate height is at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that every nonzero-normal-form branch contains a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator within the declared finite height bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: The branch termination claim is exactly the unresolved forward implication of the rational-positive separation theorem; a nonzero real-radical remainder alone does not ensure a bounded rational separator in the required sign chamber.
open_obligations.attempted: Equality-branch soundness, exact candidate checking, the search-cardinality bound, and soundness of every returned separator are proved separately. The four-node witness also proves termination on the strictness instance. These arguments do not force a qualifying table for an arbitrary nonzero branch.
open_obligations.partial_result: The equality output and every returned separator are sound by \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}bounded\text{-}search\text{-}certificate\text{-}soundness}\). The latter also proves that the prescribed rational search has at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) candidate descriptions. The explicit input \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is proved to enter the nonzero branch and return a separator by \(\mathrm{prop{:}strict\text{-}beyond\text{-}teh}\). What is not proved is that every nonzero-normal-form branch contains a qualifying rational table within the bounded list; without that assertion, exhaustion of the list need not produce either of the theorem's two advertised certificates.
